comment: Genesis activates gates that are inactive in the pinned `genesis/features.json`. Each entry identifies an intentional exception. Bank-side gates must be supported by `x/svm` (`portedBankGates`), with their effects reflected in genesis, such as setting the Rent sysvar. This file is maintained separately; `features.json` remains a faithful mainnet snapshot. The exception list is used by `x/svm`, `engine/src/conformance.rs`, and `genesis/check-features.py` to keep genesis configuration, differential tests, and drift reports consistent.

gates.name: relax_post_exec_min_balance_check
gates.why: Without it a rent-paying account cannot be credited at all unless the credit clears the whole shortfall in one transaction, so a rent raise would brick every account it strands. Rent is a number governance moves here and the ladder runs both ways.

gates.name: set_lamports_per_byte_to_6333
gates.why: Mainnet cut rent to 6,333 at slot 444,096,000, after the pin. No network runs yet, so no account exists at the old price, and a cut only accepts more: every transaction that succeeds at 6,960 succeeds at 5,080. Genesis starts at mainnet's price instead of launching with a difference nobody chose.

gates.name: set_lamports_per_byte_to_5080
gates.why: Mainnet's second cut, to 5,080, at slot 446,256,000. Genesis applies both in Agave's order, so the Rent sysvar starts at 5,080. The three cuts mainnet has not taken (2,575, 1,322, 696) stay governance decisions.

gates.name: enable_tx_v1
gates.why: Mainnet turned V1 on at slot 447,120,000, after the pin. An ephemeral rollup validator sends every commit as a V1 transaction and has no other format, so with the gate off its delegated accounts never come back. No network runs yet, so genesis turns it on instead of a governance flip 432,000 blocks after the first upgrade.
